_comment: -p/--print: non-interactive, prints final response and exits.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): the model's own text
output only, no outer transport envelope (see --json-schema below
for how the output is now additionally schema-constrained).
--permission-mode acceptEdits: auto-approve file edit/write tool
calls (the Writer role's whole job is CAN_EDIT_REPO within
allowed_files -- enforced separately by the orchestrator's scope
gate, not by this CLI flag).
--permission-prompts none: anything else that would need interactive
approval is auto-denied instead of hanging forever waiting for a
human who is not there (there is no human in a subprocess).
--json-schema (DEV-AUTO-02.4 §7): confirmed via `claude --help`
('JSON Schema for structured output validation') and a real smoke
run that, combined with --output-format text, this makes the
ENTIRE stdout exactly one JSON object matching the schema below --
no envelope, no prose, no markdown fences -- while real tool use
(Read/Bash) still happens normally before that final answer. This
directly fixes a real D0103 Writer run that returned its result
inside a ```json fenced code block, which the strict last-line
parser correctly rejected (fail closed, not a parser bug). The
schema mirrors WriterResult.from_raw_output()'s exact contract
(agent_results.py) -- not a new/looser contract.
--allowedTools (DEV-AUTO-02.3, narrowed in DEV-AUTO-02.4 §1):
git status/diff/rev-parse only now. DEV-AUTO-02.3 also allowed
Bash(python *)/Bash(ruff *)/Bash(mypy *) so the Writer could run
manifest.targeted_tests/static_checks itself, but a real D0103 run
showed this was still broken in practice: the Writer's own
Noninteractive Claude CLI subprocess only sees the global Python
3.14 PATH, not this repository's `.venv` -- pytest happened to be
on the global PATH too so it ran, but ruff/mypy were not, so they
silently could not run at all. DEV-AUTO-02.4 fixes this
architecturally instead of by further expanding Agent shell
permissions: manifest.targeted_tests/static_checks are now
executed by the HOST orchestrator itself (host_validation.py,
repo_root as cwd, so repo-relative `.venv\Scripts\...` paths
resolve correctly -- see the D0103 pilot manifest), and the
Writer prompt no longer asks the Agent to run them at all. Only
git status/diff/rev-parse remain allowed, for the Writer's
'inspect' responsibility (DEV-AUTO-02.4 §1).
--disallowedTools: explicit tool-level denial of every git-mutation
subcommand, even though `Bash(git *)` is deliberately NOT used as
the allow pattern (git allow-list above is scoped to
status/diff/rev-parse only). This is defense-in-depth on top of
that scoping and on top of the Writer prompt's own 'you may not
commit, push, or independently declare acceptance' instruction
(do not rely solely on prompt instructions for destructive
operations when a tool-level restriction is available). Confirmed
empirically (DEV-AUTO-02.3) that an explicit --disallowedTools
entry overrides a broader --allowedTools match for the same
command. Writer's own capability set (CAN_EDIT_REPO, CAN_RUN_TESTS
-- see model.py ROLE_CAPABILITIES) has neither CAN_COMMIT nor
CAN_PUSH, so add/commit/push/checkout/reset/clean/branch are all
denied unconditionally (Writer never legitimately needs any of
them).
Compound/chained commands (`cmd1; cmd2`, `cmd1 && cmd2`) are NOT
matched by these simple prefix rules and are auto-denied as a
side effect (confirmed empirically, DEV-AUTO-02.3) -- an
incidental but useful defense, not relied upon as the primary
protection; the explicit --disallowedTools entries above are.
Prompt is appended as the trailing positional argument by
LocalCommandExecutor (prompt_via=arg), matching `claude`'s
`[options] [command] [prompt]` usage.
Separate invocation/process from the Writer, with its own reviewer
prompt (build_reviewer_prompt / build_closure_reviewer_prompt) that
explicitly instructs READ ONLY behavior.
--output-format text (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): same reasoning as the Writer
above (see --json-schema below for the additional structured-
output constraint).
--permission-mode dontAsk (DEV-AUTO-02.3, was `plan`): `plan` mode
was tried first but empirically deadlocks this noninteractive
setup (required writing a plan file to ~/.claude/plans/... with
no Write tool available -- an approval state nobody could answer).
`dontAsk` avoids this while still fully respecting
--permission-prompts none and the --allowedTools/--disallowedTools
rules below.
--json-schema (DEV-AUTO-02.4 §7): same mechanism and reasoning as
the Writer's above, confirmed empirically under this Reviewer's
own --restricted/--tools/--permission-mode combination too (real
tool use still happens; the final stdout is exactly one JSON
object with no envelope/prose/fencing). Schema mirrors
ReviewerResult.from_raw_output()'s exact contract (agent_results.py
+ Finding.from_dict in model.py) -- not a new/looser contract.
--restricted --tools Bash: `--restricted` alone removes Bash
entirely; `--tools Bash` restores only the Bash tool while keeping
every other --restricted protection intact (ignores
user/project/local settings files, confines file tools to the
working directory, refuses bypassPermissions, gates writes to
settings/git/tool-config files to a human/permission handler).
--allowedTools (DEV-AUTO-02.3, narrowed in DEV-AUTO-02.4 §1): git
status/diff/rev-parse only now. DEV-AUTO-02.3 also allowed
Bash(python *)/Bash(ruff *)/Bash(mypy *) so the Reviewer's nominal
CAN_RUN_TESTS capability (model.py ROLE_CAPABILITIES) could
actually execute -- but DEV-AUTO-02.4 moves ALL manifest
targeted_tests/static_checks execution to the HOST orchestrator
(host_validation.py), which injects the results directly into
this Reviewer's prompt (see build_reviewer_prompt in prompts.py).
The Reviewer no longer needs to (and no longer may) run
pytest/ruff/mypy itself -- it independently judges the semantics
of the change and whether the Host-supplied validation results are
sufficient evidence, restoring a truthful CAN_REVIEW_READ_ONLY
without a contradictory shell-execution permission. Only
git status/diff/rev-parse remain allowed, for the Reviewer's
'read-only inspect diff/code' responsibility.
--disallowedTools Edit,Write,MultiEdit,NotebookEdit,git-mutation:
explicit defense-in-depth denial of every file-mutation tool AND
every git-mutation subcommand (add/commit/push/checkout/reset/
clean/branch), on top of --restricted itself (Edit/Write/
MultiEdit/NotebookEdit are not even in --tools, so this is a
second, redundant-by-design layer for those four), and the
orchestrator's own git-state diff comparison below. Reviewer has
no CAN_EDIT_REPO/CAN_COMMIT/CAN_PUSH capability at all (see
model.py ROLE_CAPABILITIES) -- none of these denials removes
anything the Reviewer legitimately needs.
--permission-prompts none: same non-interactive fail-closed reason
as the Writer.
-- (DEV-AUTO-02.2.1): required end-of-options marker. Any of the
variadic list flags above (--tools/--allowedTools/
--disallowedTools) would otherwise swallow the prompt string
that LocalCommandExecutor appends after this command array
(prompt_via=arg) as extra (bogus) list entries instead of reading
it as the prompt.
Compound/chained commands (`cmd1; cmd2`, `cmd1 && cmd2`) are NOT
matched by the --allowedTools prefix rules and are auto-denied as
a side effect (confirmed empirically, DEV-AUTO-02.3) -- not
relied upon as the primary protection.
This CLI-level restriction is a second, independent layer on top of
the orchestrator's own pre/post git-state diff comparison in
orchestrator.py, which rejects the reviewer's verdict outright if the
repository was modified during the reviewer's execution -- so
read-only is enforced even if a future CLI flag change loosens the
options above.
